name: Thought Bulb Wishlist for WooCommerce
author: Agentmatica

sections.description:
Thought Bulb Wishlist lets shoppers save products for later, share their list with friends and family, and come back to buy.

Built for speed and caching

  • Pages stay fully cacheable: the heart buttons light up after the page loads.
  • Guests’ wishlists live in their own browser (localStorage) by default, with no database rows and no cookies. They move into the account automatically on login.
  • Custom indexed database tables, not post meta.
  • No ?add_to_wishlist= links for bots to crawl. The wishlist page, shared lists included, is marked noindex and nofollow, so search engines skip it.

Everything shoppers expect, free

  • Heart button on product pages and shop grids (on the image, after the title or price, or next to Add to cart).
  • Heart counter for your header menu, shown as the heart, heart and text, or text only.
  • Multiple wishlists with a “Save to…” picker.
  • Share with one tap: the phone’s share sheet (iMessage, WhatsApp, Mail…), or Copy link, Email, WhatsApp, SMS, Telegram, Facebook, X and Pinterest on desktop.
  • Shared lists are read-only, with “Add all to cart” for gifts and registries. Products that need a choice first, such as a size, are left out and the shopper is told which ones, as are out-of-stock items.
  • Shared lists show what is already bought (“Already bought”, or “1 of 2 bought”), so two people don’t buy the same gift. The list owner doesn’t see it, so gifts stay a surprise.
  • My Account → Wishlist tab.
  • Guests can use the wishlist, or you can ask them to log in first. Guest lists kept on the server are deleted after 30 days by default (you choose how long).
  • Blocks: Wishlist, Add to Wishlist Button, Wishlist Counter. Shortcodes: [tbww_wishlist], [tbww_button], [tbww_count].
  • “Theme default” appearance that blends into your theme, or pick your own color, icon (heart, star or bookmark) and size with a live preview.
  • Works with block themes and classic themes, HPOS, and Cart/Checkout blocks.

For store managers

  • Wishlists screen: search your customers’ lists by name or email, open a list, see imported lists waiting for sign-up, or delete one.
  • A sortable “Wishlisted” count column on the Products list.
  • Dashboard with saved items, wishlists, customers with a wishlist and the most wished-for products.
  • A built-in Help guide, and an ⓘ explanation on every settings section.

Move your data in and out

  • CSV import with column matching, a dry-run test and a results report. It works with exports from any wishlist app.
  • Customers without an account yet get their imported wishlist when they sign up with the same email.
  • CSV export (also a backup you can import again).
  • Optional exact-title matching and custom Shopify product ID fields, and a report that lists products that weren’t found.
  • WP-CLI: wp tbww import (with --dry-run and --skip-guests), wp tbww export, wp tbww stats.

Privacy

  • Works with WordPress’s Export/Erase Personal Data tools.
  • Suggested privacy policy text included.

For developers

  • A REST API under tbww/v1 for the shopper’s lists and items, used by the plugin’s own scripts.
  • Filters and actions such as tbww_show_button, tbww_single_positions, tbww_loop_positions, tbww_max_lists_per_owner and tbww_item_added.

Source code

The admin screens are a React app. Its readable source is included in the plugin’s src/ folder; rebuild build/ with npm install && npm run build.

TB Wishlist Pro

TB Wishlist Pro turns wishlists into sales:

  • Automatic price-drop and back-in-stock emails, plus almost-sold-out emails you can turn on, with an optional coupon. Alerts go to shoppers with an account, and to guests who leave their email under their wishlist and confirm it.
  • Revenue analytics: orders and revenue that started on a wishlist.
  • One-click migration from Shopify apps (Growave, Swym, Swish / Wishlist King, Hulk, Pasilobus, customer metafields) and from YITH or TI wishlists.

External services

This plugin works fully without any external service. One feature connects to an outside service, and only after a store manager opts in:

Setup emails from Thought Bulb (optional). On the plugin’s Dashboard, a store manager can choose to receive setup tips and reminder emails. Nothing is sent unless they tick the consent box and click Subscribe. After that, when a setup milestone happens (subscribing, the first product saved to a wishlist, the first import, Pro activated, plugin activated or deactivated), the plugin sends the subscribed email address, first name, the site’s name, URL and admin URL, country, language, plugin version and the milestone dates to Thought Bulb at https://thoughtbulb.dev/api/tbww/v1/lifecycle. Thought Bulb passes them to its email provider Loops (loops.so), which sends the emails. No shopper or wishlist data is ever sent. Unsubscribe any time from the plugin’s Dashboard or from any email.

  • Thought Bulb: Terms, Privacy policy
  • Loops: Terms, Privacy policy

Site owners can disable this completely with define( 'TBWW_DISABLE_LIFECYCLE_EMAILS', true ); in wp-config.php.

Share buttons are plain links to the chosen network (Facebook, X, Pinterest, WhatsApp, Telegram, email or SMS). They only open when a shopper clicks them, and no scripts from those services are loaded.
sections.installation:
1. Install and activate WooCommerce.
  2. Install Thought Bulb Wishlist from Plugins → Add New, or upload the zip.
  3. Go to WooCommerce → Wishlist. A “Wishlist” page has already been created for you.
sections.faq:
Does it work with page caching?

Yes. The HTML is identical for everyone; button states are filled in by a small script after load.

Where are guest wishlists stored?

By default in the shopper’s browser, with no cookie. You can switch to server storage under Settings → Guests & storage; server storage recognises guests with a first-party cookie.

Can a guest see their wishlist on another device?

Not while it is stored in their browser: a list saved on a phone stays on that phone. Once the guest logs in or signs up, the list moves into their account and shows on every device they sign in on.

Can I move wishlists from Shopify?

Yes. Export the CSV from your Shopify wishlist app and use Import & Export → CSV file. Pro adds presets and API connections for the most popular apps.

What happens to variable products under “Add all to cart”?

A saved variation (for example “Sweater – Medium”) goes in the cart like any other product. A variable product saved without a choice shows “Select options” and isn’t added; the shopper sees a list of what wasn’t added, with links, before going to the cart. Out-of-stock items are listed the same way.

How does a shared list know what’s been bought?

When someone adds items to the cart from a shared list and places the order, the items are counted as bought once the order is on hold, processing or completed. If the order is cancelled, refunded or fails, the count goes back down. “Add all to cart” skips items that are fully bought.

Can I change the templates?

Copy any file from templates/ to yourtheme/tb-wishlist/.
sections.changelog:
1.1.0

  • Shared lists show which items have already been bought, so gift buyers don’t buy the same thing twice. Hidden from the list owner. “Add all to cart” skips bought items.
  • “Add all to cart” now lists the items it couldn’t add (products that need options chosen, out of stock, no longer available) instead of going straight to the cart.

1.0.3

  • Readme: says who gets the Pro price-drop and back-in-stock emails, and that the whole wishlist page is marked noindex and nofollow.

1.0.2

  • Add-ons can now add content under a guest’s wishlist when it is kept in the browser (tbww_after_wishlist runs there too).
  • FAQ: where guest wishlists are kept, and seeing them on another device.

1.0.1

  • Fix: the share dialog keeps its layout on themes that restyle every button and text field (Copy link button no longer cut off, share buttons all the same size).

1.0.0

  • First release.
